newsitem.title: POLAND: Flood to boost Polish rapeseed imports to 500,000T.
newsitem.headline: Flood to boost Polish rapeseed imports to 500,000T.

text.p: Flood damage to crops may boost Poland's rapeseed imports to 500,000 tonnes this year but some fat-processing companies said they might import raw soybean oil instead, industry officials said on Monday.

Jan Bielecki from the government-linked Agriculture Economics Institute told Reuters Polish rapeseed crops this year were likely to fall to 300,000-350,000 tonnes from the earlier estimated 400,000-440,000 tonnes because of the recent flooding.

"Imports of oilseeds and raw oil would be high even without the flood damage and were estimated at 400,000 tonnes. But taking into account the flood losses, imports my rise to 500,000 tonnes," Bielecki said.
"Rapeseed output is likely to be 300,000-350,000 tonnes, depending on the weather during harvesting," he said.
In 1996 Poland produced some 500,000 tonnes of rapeseed with domestic demand estimated at 850,000-900,000 tonnes.
Weeks of rain at the start of July caused floods in southern Poland which inundated almost 5,000 square kilometres, killing 52 people so far and forcing tens of thousands out of their homes.
The precise impact of the floods on Poland's agriculture production is not yet known, but harvesting has been delayed for two to three weeks.

Some fat-processing companies said the gap between supply and demand would not necessarily be filled with rapeseed imports, as some firms could switch their production lines to process raw soybean oil instead.
The rapeseed import duty is currently 15 percent while raw soybean oil duty is 10 percent.

"If everybody processes rapeseed, we will need imports of about 500,000 tonnes, but the figure may be much lower if some process soybean oil," said Mieczyslaw Parzydlo, manager in fat-processing Zaklady Przemyslu Tluszczowego in Warsaw.

Analysts said currently the two biggest Polish fat-processing companies, ZPT Olvit in Gdansk and Kruszwica could switch to soybean processing and cut the expected rapeseed imports by 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
Andrzej Gorski, a manager in ZPT Olvit, told Reuters, however, that his company wanted to process rapeseed and would lobby for a duty-free import quota.
"We are interested in processing domestic and imported rapeseed. The government should introduce a duty-free import quota for rapeseed," Gorski said. --Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
